headline: House passes Senate-amended S.2155, raising the SIFI prudential threshold from $50B to $250B
why_this_event_is_defensible: S.2155 raised the SIFI prudential threshold from $50B in assets to $250B, removing enhanced prudential standards (stress testing, capital planning, liquidity rules) for mid-size regional banks. ZION had roughly $66B in assets at the time, placing it cleanly inside the threshold band that the bill relieved. KBE controls for broader bank-sector reaction.
what_would_falsify: ZION does not outperform KBE; broader bank sector reacts uniformly (no threshold-band differentiation); law was already fully priced by the March 14 Senate passage and the May 22 House vote behaves as a formality; macro/rate moves dominate.
operator_notes: Use 2018-05-22 (House passes the Senate-amended bill) rather than the May 24 ceremonial signing — May 22 is the last legislative-uncertainty event. ZION is a KBE constituent; this is the standard sector-controlled event-study setup, and the constituent-in-benchmark bias is small (constituent weight × constituent move) for single-name-vs-broad-sector tests. The same shape applies to the other sector-benchmark rows in this batch. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.

headline: U.S. Commerce Department adds Huawei Technologies to the Entity List, restricting U.S. component exports
why_this_event_is_defensible: Commerce announced the Entity List designation evening of May 15, 2019; first full equity session reflecting the news was May 16. Lumentum had publicly disclosed Huawei as a significant customer (roughly 11 percent of revenue at designation) and U.S. export-control rules restricted continued shipment of its 3D-sensing and optical components. SMH controls for broader semiconductor-sector reaction.
what_would_falsify: LITE does not underperform SMH; market had already priced the designation before May 15; Huawei substitutes U.S. components quickly; alternative customers offset; broader semi sell-off explains the move.
operator_notes: First market session after the May 15 evening Commerce announcement is May 16. LITE was reshaped by the Oclaro acquisition (closed December 2018), so the pre-event 60-bar estimation window from mid-February 2019 onward sits entirely within the post-Oclaro corporate form. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.

headline: Philadelphia Energy Solutions (PES) refinery permanently shut after June 21 fire; East-Coast refining capacity reduced
why_this_event_is_defensible: The fire at PES on Friday June 21, 2019 destroyed the largest refinery on the U.S. East Coast (about 335 kbpd of capacity). PES, already in bankruptcy, announced permanent closure within days. PBF operates the Delaware City and Paulsboro refineries in the same East-Coast PADD 1 region; removal of a major regional competitor concentrates pricing power among the remaining East-Coast refiners. CRAK controls for broader refining-sector reaction.
what_would_falsify: PBF does not outperform CRAK; market reads the fire as transient and expects PES restart under a new operator; broader refining-sector moves explain the response; structural East-Coast refining unprofitability dominates the competitive-capacity-removal story; product imports backfill the lost capacity quickly.
operator_notes: First full market session after the Friday June 21 fire is Monday June 24, when PBF reacted to news of permanent closure. PBF is a CRAK constituent; standard sector-controlled setup. Distinct ticker pair from the prior manual-five batch (no overlap with UGA/USO from the Colonial row). Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.

headline: President signs Section 201 safeguard proclamation imposing tariffs on imported large residential washers
why_this_event_is_defensible: Whirlpool was the original Section 201 petitioner. The safeguard proclamation, signed evening of January 22, 2018, imposed declining-rate tariffs on imported washers (50 percent for the first 1.2 million units, 20 percent thereafter in year one) — a direct industrial-policy support aimed at Korean (LG, Samsung) and Chinese imports Whirlpool competed against. XLY controls for broader consumer-discretionary reaction.
what_would_falsify: WHR does not outperform XLY; Korean producers shift production to U.S. plants quickly (LG/Samsung U.S. plants in Tennessee and South Carolina were already under construction at the time); cost pass-through to consumers depresses unit demand; broader consumer-discretionary moves explain the response.
operator_notes: First full market session after the January 22 evening signing is January 23. WHR is an XLY constituent; standard sector-controlled setup. Pre-existing announced U.S. capacity from LG/Samsung weakens the long-window read; the short-window read is the cleaner test. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.

headline: U.S. Treasury / OFAC sanctions Rusal, EN+ Group, and Oleg Deripaska, disrupting global aluminum supply
why_this_event_is_defensible: Treasury announced sanctions on Rusal and EN+ Group during U.S. market hours on Friday April 6, 2018. Rusal was the world second-largest aluminum producer; the sanctions disrupted Rusal access to U.S. counterparties and triggered a sharp LME aluminum price spike. Century Aluminum (CENX) is a pure-play U.S. primary-aluminum smelter that benefits directly from tighter global aluminum supply and higher LME aluminum prices. XME (metals and mining ETF) controls for broader metals-sector reaction.
what_would_falsify: CENX does not outperform XME; OFAC walks back enforcement (which began with the April 23, 2018 license extensions and led to sanctions being lifted in January 2019), diluting the post-event window; broader metals-sector moves dominate; the aluminum-price spike does not translate to CENX margin expansion.
operator_notes: OFAC announcement was during market hours on April 6, so April 6 is the event date. CENX listed in 1996 with continuous coverage — no spin-off or IPO-window discontinuity. XME includes substantial steel exposure and the same Q1-2018 window carried Section 232 steel-tariff news (March 8, 2018), so XME is partially contaminated by an adjacent industrial-policy story; that contamination affects steel constituents rather than the aluminum-specific signal CENX is intended to test. The 20-day post-event window is materially diluted by the April 23 enforcement walk-back — short-window (1-day, 5-day) reads are cleaner than the 20-day read. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.
